sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Global Payroll and Staff Compliance Software

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 as amended by Law No. 2023-451 of 9 June 2023 implementing 5th AML Directive); UBO register governed by Articles L. 233-3 et seq. of the Code de commerce and Decree No. 2020-1617 of 21 December 2020

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Infogreffe

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statuts de la Société à Responsabilité Limitée

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic (Trésor Public) screening of directors, beneficial owners, and related parties using official lists

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of French language and Latin alphabet; no transliteration permitted for French company names
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying public authority or monopoly (e.g., Banque, Assurance, État)
Words misleading as to corporate purpose
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the Président du Tribunal de Commerce within two months of rejection; subsequent recourse possible to administrative courts

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for registered office provided it is a verifiable physical address in France for correspondence and tax purposes; virtual-only setups subject to verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal consultation, name reservation, and incorporation filing fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for SARL formation services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and consular legalization of documents
UBO registration, beneficial ownership due diligence, and PEP/sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff or prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq. (SARL); Civil Code Articles 1832 and 1845; derived from Directive (EU) 2017/1132
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) in the jurisdiction of the registered office; filing centralised via Infogreffe
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (articles of association) and Cerfa No. M0 business registration application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum legal capital; capital is fixed in the statutes. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation and deposited in a blocked escrow account with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; in-kind contributions require a commissaire aux apports report if the value exceeds EUR 30,000 or represents more than 50% of the capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders of FR SARL, acting on [date], resolve as follows: (1) The share capital of EUR [amount] is subscribed in full by each shareholder listed in the attendance sheet, divided into shares, and paid up as provided by law; funds have been deposited in a blocked account. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], in the jurisdiction of the Registry of the Commercial Court. (3) [Name] is appointed as single manager (gérant) for an indefinite term, with power to represent the company and to exercise all management powers within the corporate object. (4) The manager is authorised to complete all formalities, sign the publication notice, and file the incorporation application with the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and drafting of the statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via data.inpi.fr for name/trademark availability; legal counsel or online legal platform for statutory drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify corporate name availability and register a trademark if commercial branding protection is required; draft the statutes indicating corporate form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, social purpose, and management structure; obtain signatures from all shareholders, in person or by electronic signature compliant with eIDAS.
required_dossiers: Certified identity documents of each shareholder
Statement of business purpose and ISIC/NAICS alignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing trademark or corporate name, amend the proposed name or file a new trademark clearance request; if the statutes are rejected by a bank or notary, revise the relevant clauses and recirculate for signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) acting as depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation; deposit the full cash portion of the share capital; obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds issued by the depositary, stating the amount deposited and the account details; retain this certificate for later submission to the registry.
required_dossiers: Certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Source of funds evidence for AML/KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary requests additional KYC information, provide prompt documentation; if the bank refuses the deposit due to incomplete corporate documentation, select another licensed depositary or complete the missing statutory elements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal publication of the incorporation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcements newspaper (journal d'annonces légales) authorised in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and publish the incorporation notice containing the company name, French legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office, corporate object, managers, and the commercial court registration number once assigned; obtain the certificate of publication issued by the gazette.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if publication is filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication notice is rejected or contains errors, correct the text and re-submit; use an alternative approved legal gazette in the same department if timing becomes critical.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation dossier with the commercial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing via Infogreffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Cerfa M0 form, signed statutes, capital deposit certificate, proof of legal publication, evidence of registered office, identity documents of managers, and compliance declarations; pay the registration fee; the registry will issue the K-bis extract and the Siren/Siret number upon approval.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or domiciliation contract for registered office
Proof of legal publication in a licensed gazette
Identity documents of shareholders and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a demande de complément (enquiry for additional information), respond within the prescribed period, usually 15 days, by completing the missing documents or correcting inconsistencies; re-file electronically through Infogreffe without additional delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the company with INSEE and post-filing clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques (INSEE) via automatic transmission from the Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Greffe approves the filing, INSEE automatically allocates the Siren, Siret and NAF code; verify the K-bis extract ensures that the French legal form, corporate name, share capital and registered office are correctly recorded; obtain a formal K-bis and use it for bank account activation and tax registrations.
required_dossiers: Extract of K-bis issued after incorporation
Manager identity and proof of domicile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Siren or Siret is not received within the expected SLA, contact the Greffe to confirm transmission to INSEE; if the K-bis shows inaccurate data, file an application for rectification with the Greffe.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure SaaS activity; if a physical office is established, the competent authority is the DRIEETS (Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités) for occupational health and safety, and the local Préfecture for any premises-related permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license required for ISIC 6201 computer programming and payroll SaaS activities under French law; a simple occupational declaration is sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (Évaluation Environnementale)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — administrative registration not required; office-based software activity is outside the scope of Article R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code requiring a formal EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliant with the general obligations of the EU Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC); office wastewater must be discharged into the municipal sewer network per public health code standards; any equipment containing batteries or electronic components must be disposed through registered WEEE channels; energy consumption must follow the French Environmental Code and the Grenelle II regulations on digital sustainability.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) is required for any office premises open to employees or customers; a structural load inspection is not needed for standard commercial leases, but workplace electrical and ventilation certificates are mandatory under the French Labor Code (Articles R.4222-1 and R.4227-1 et seq.); occupational clearance is evidenced by a formal health and safety risk assessment (document unique) maintained in the workplace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — French General Directorate of Public Finances, Ministry of Economy and Finance; online portal: impots.gouv.fr; company registration portal: guichet-entreprises.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL, incorporation is filed online through the Guichet Unique (formalités entreprises); INSEE then issues SIREN and SIRET numbers, and DGFiP automatically allocates a French intra-community VAT number (FR + key + SIREN) to established taxable persons. A foreign entity with no French establishment deriving taxable supplies from France must apply for a French VAT number by filing Form CA16 with the DGFiP (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) and, where applicable, use the non-Union OSS or Union OSS scheme for distance sales and certain B2C services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a French SARL is the legal taxpayer for French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) on its worldwide profits when tax resident in France; non-resident entities remain taxable in France only to the extent of a French permanent establishment or stabilized French-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under French law. A SARL may in limited cases opt for pass-through taxation as a société de personnes, notably a SARL de famille (CGI Art. 239) when all partners are within the same family, or, for certain eligible small enterprises, under Article 239 bis AA for a five-year corporate income tax option; elections are filed with the DGFiP and are subject to statutory conditions. Hybrid mismatch recategorizations under EU ATAD are mandatory and automatic, not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For businesses established in France, the small-business exemption/toleration threshold is EUR 85,000 for goods and EUR 37,500 for services; foreign entities making taxable French supplies must register without any local turnover franche, except that intra-EU cross-border distance sales of goods benefit from an annual EUR 10,000 OSS threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) and e-reporting to the DGFiP are being phased in from 1 September 2026 through 2027 via the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); invoices must be transmitted through an immatriculated dematerialization platform or the PPF API. France does not use pre-clearance digital stamping; instead, e-reporting data is transmitted near-real-time and subjected to automated audit risk-scoring algorithms.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical export of goods from France to a destination outside the EU is zero-rated at 0% VAT if the supplier retains sufficient documentary proof of actual export and the goods are removed from France within the statutory timeline; certain services directly connected to exported goods, and services supplied B2B to non-EU recipients under the French place-of-supply rules, may also qualify for zero-rating or placement outside the scope of French VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / DAU) with movement reference number
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note
Commercial invoice and customs value evidence
Proof of receipt of consideration / inward remittance certificate or bank swift
Export register with commodity code, exporter, consignee, destination and dates
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP may retrospectively reverse export zero-rating within the standard three-year assessment period, extended to six years for hidden activities or offshore havens; if export documentation is missing, misleading or false, the VAT is clawed back at 20% plus monthly late-payment interest, and a 40% bad-faith penalty or 80% abusive-practice penalty may be applied; severe fraud and customs misdeclaration may attract criminal fines up to the value of the goods and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor for external financial relations and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking and AML/CFT supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in France for both current account and capital account transactions under TFEU Articles 63-66. No exchange-control authorization, currency quota, or mandatory conversion applies to software export receipts, client invoicing, inbound equity injections, intra-group loans, or profit remittances. Dividends and other profit distributions to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted from an FX perspective, but banks require standard AML/KYC evidence, a tax residence certificate, current SARL Kbis, corporate authorization, and, where treaty relief is claimed, appropriate withholding-tax documentation. Existing limitations are limited to EU/UN financial sanctions, asset freezes, and temporary safeguard measures under Article 66 TFEU.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation, or conversion requirement for export proceeds. There is no mandatory timeline and no minimum conversion ratio; the effective required conversion ratio is 0%. Exporters may keep foreign currency abroad for legitimate treasury needs. French resident credit institutions are required to capture cross-border transactions for the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical returns; for typical SMEs this reporting is performed via the bank rather than by the exporting company itself.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency treasury clearing and SWIFT settlement account
Cross-border trade settlement and foreign-currency transactional account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions passporting into France under PSD2 through an ACPR notification; Low/Nil for offshore digital EMIs based outside the EEA or relying on a revoked UK passport. An offshore EMI cannot legally maintain a French SARL payroll account or hold client funds because it lacks authorization under Article L.521-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code. An EU-licensed EMI may be used as an ancillary non-settlement rail for high-speed, low-value SEPA contractor payouts, but the master payroll account and payroll-fund custody must remain at an ACPR-licensed credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto mandatory at French Tier-1 banks. Although French law permits remote onboarding through an eIDAS-qualified electronic signature and an ACPR-compliant video-identification procedure, most established banks still require the SARL legal representative and material UBOs to appear physically at least once before account activation. Original passports, residence permits, extrait Kbis, and UBO registration documents must be presented. The treasury plan should budget for a physical interview in France unless a specific bank has confirmed in writing that its digital onboarding platform will be accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capitalisation from a non-resident parent or third-party brokerage/crypto account without visible economic basis for a low-capital SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share subscription minutes; bank statements from the remitter; signed source-of-wealth declaration for each UBO; remuneration or sale/proceeds evidence; tax residence certificates; fund path audit file; notarised or apostilled corporate resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-jurisdictional ownership with trusts, nominee shareholders, or UBOs resident in high-risk territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extrait Kbis; Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs filing; full organisational chart; UBO identification forms with passports and proof of address; CRS/FATCA self-certifications; written commercial rationale; substance documentation for intermediate holding entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll disbursement pattern diverging from declared purpose, including round-trip transfers, frequent non-beneficiary third-party payments, or sanctions-listed counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master services agreement; payroll-beneficiary aggregate register; redacted payslips; employment classification legal opinion; vendor invoices with proof of delivery; sanctions-screening policy and match-resolution case files; AML training records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Platform may be viewed as an unauthorised payment institution or remittance provider if client payroll funds are commingled in the French SARL account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent French legal opinion on PSD2 scope and Article L.521-1 et seq.; no-holding-of-client-funds flow diagram; account segregation and service agreement with an ACPR-licensed credit institution; ACPR passport or registration evidence, or agency agreements with a licensed payment institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, PEP status, or prior regulatory enforcement involving a director, UBO, or material payroll client.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP/adverse-media questionnaire; commercial due diligence report; case-specific negative-news evidence and resolution documents; explanation of underlying transactions; senior compliance committee approval; enhanced transaction-monitoring undertaking.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For EUR capital contributions from an EU/EEA shareholder, use a SEPA Credit Transfer in ISO 20022 pain.001 with the bank-specific purpose code for 'capital increase / dépôt de fonds' or, where the bank accepts it, Category Purpose INTC for intra-company payments. For USD, GBP, or non-EEA inbound funding, use SWIFT MT103 or MT103 COV where intermediary banks are involved. The remittance information must explicitly state 'FR_SARL capital injection / share subscription'; it must not describe the payment as goods, services, or fees. Delivery documents include notarised subscription minutes for capital increases, updated UBO registration, current extrait Kbis, shareholder resolution, source-of-funds file, and, if applicable, a shareholder loan agreement with documented arm's-length terms. The French receiving bank will classify the transaction for Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001 via EBICS) for euro-denominated payroll disbursements; SEPA Direct Debit Core/B2B for collecting client payroll funding; SWIFT MT103 for cross-border USD/GBP payments to contractors and non-EEA vendors; FedACH/CHIPS via a US correspondent bank for actual USD payroll nodes; and Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit under UCP 600/ISBP 745 for any physical or trade-related imports, opened by SWIFT MT700 with compliant presentation instructions. Every outbound file must be sanctions-screened before release and must carry a clear payment purpose, for example 'net salaries', 'payroll taxes', 'software license fee', or 'vendor invoice'.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (change à terme) for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and other convertible payroll currencies, documented under ISDA 2002, French MAF, or a bank treasury line.
FX swaps (swap de change) for converting surplus EUR into short-term disbursement currencies and reversing the transaction before settlement.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps to hedge long-term shareholder loans or cross-border financing and to match payroll currency cash-flow liabilities.
Currency options, including FX call/put options, zero-premium collars, and risk-reversal structures, provided the position is genuinely hedging forecast payroll commitments and is not speculative.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for currencies of jurisdictions with local non-convertibility, offshore settlement restrictions, or limited deliverability; settlements are net EUR/USD and are subject to ACPR conduct rules, EMIR trade reporting, and documented payroll/tax exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale), comprising Form 2065 and annexes 2053 to 2058
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) via the mandatory electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal years ending 31 December, file no later than the second business day after 1 May (typically 3 May). For other fiscal year-ends, file within three months of the closing date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic tax assessment if the return is not filed; late-payment penalty of 5% of corporate income tax, increased to 10% after 30 days; monthly interest at 0.40% (intérêt de retard) accrues on unpaid taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels), including balance sheet, profit and loss account, annexes and, where required, management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet unique acting for the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Greffe du tribunal de commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the accounts within six months of the fiscal year-end; the approved accounts must be filed within one month of approval, giving a final statutory deadline of the last day of the seventh month after the balance-sheet date. The Commercial Court may grant an extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court may order the filing under a daily periodic fine (astreinte); directors may be subject to civil fines; persistent non-filing may lead to loss of the RCS extract, ineligibility for certain contracts, and eventual administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner register review and, if any change occurred, updated declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) via the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate annual filing is required if the beneficial-owner information is unchanged; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days after the event. In practice the declaration is reviewed and, if necessary, updated together with the annual accounts filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the UBO declaration within 30 days exposes the legal entity to an administrative fine of up to EUR 5,000, may suspend voting rights, and may trigger a separate court order requiring rectification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Articles L. 823-12 and R. 823-1 of the French Commercial Code, a SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at the balance-sheet date, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total balance sheet greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,000,000; average permanent headcount greater than 50 in the fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Standalone SARL statutory accounts are prepared in accordance with French GAAP, set out in the Plan Comptable Général (PCG / ANC Regulation 2014-03, as amended). Consolidated accounts of groups and listed companies are prepared under IFRS as adopted by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a separate annual UBO renewal filing. The SARL must keep the RBE declaration current and accurate; any shareholding transfer or other event changing beneficial ownership triggers a mandatory update within 30 days. The annual accounts filing and shareholders' meeting serve as practical checkpoints for confirming that the recorded UBO information remains correct.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managers (registre des gérants)
Minute Book (registre des procès-verbaux et feuilles de présence)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – USD 650 per annum for professional domiciliation services in France (approximately EUR 170 – EUR 600), depending on city and service level.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500 – USD 18,000 (approximately EUR 6,000 – EUR 17,000) for a mandatory statutory audit of a small to medium SARL when thresholds are exceeded; voluntary review engagements typically range from USD 3,000 – USD 6,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate; 15% reduced rate on the first €42,500 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for SMEs up to €42,500 profit; Research Tax Credit (Crédit Impôt Recherche) and Innovation Tax Credit; Jeune Entreprise Innovante (JEI) exemption (partial or full) for up to 5 years; no general statutory tax holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD plus annexes 2050-SD to 2058-SD; filed online via the impots.gouv.fr professional portal (EFI/EDI procedure)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending 31 December, the return is due by midnight on the date published by the administration in May of the following year (typically 3 May for online filers); for other fiscal year-ends, within three months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the net taxable income after adjustment of accounting profit (add non-deductible expenses, deduct profits/losses of operations allocated to France).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a foreign company carries on a business in France through a permanent establishment, include only the PE's attributable income and expenses; losses of the foreign head office may not be set off against French PE profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Frame 15 - Déficits ordinaires reportables (ordinary deficit carryforward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report prior-year deficits used against current-year taxable profits, respecting the annual cap of €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding €1,000,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies can offset deficits incurred within the French PE, but losses from their home country cannot be used in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter tax credits such as Crédit Impôt Recherche, foreign tax credits taken under a DTA, and other recoverable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the TRC and detail supporting the credit; non-residents may claim refunds on form 2065 if a French PE exists; taxes withheld at source on French income may be credited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report intercompany transactions with related entities, including cost-sharing arrangements and IP services, required for transfer-pricing assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent with French subsidiary or PE must ensure that Master File/Local File documentation is available to the French tax authorities on demand.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge (spontaneous correction) or 40% after formal demand (80% for illegal activity); monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%; additional €10,000 fine for non-electronic filing; parallel criminal penalties in cases of fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under domestic law (CGI Article 119 bis); reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (≥10% holding for two years) and to treaty rates (e.g., 0-15%) under applicable DTA; 75% if paid to a non-cooperative jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must provide a tax residence certificate (TRC) and submit the relevant French treaty relief form (e.g., form 5004 for parent-subsidiary directive) to the French paying agent before the payment; alternatively, claim a refund from the French tax authorities (SIE) within the statutory limitation period, attaching proof of beneficial ownership, residence, and no abusive conduit arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory withholding, 0% under EU Interest and Royalties Directive, 0-5% under most DTAs. Interest: generally exempt from withholding to EU or treaty-resident lenders, but 25% statutory for disqualified cases; 75% to non-cooperative territories; typical DTA interest rate 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The obligation to prepare and file transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) applies where the annual consolidated group revenue or total assets exceed EUR 400,000,000; smaller entities must nevertheless provide basic documentation on request.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the OECD arm's-length principle and a substance-over-form approach; a discrete Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) statute is not in force, but an entity lacking business substance, employees, premises, and local management is exposed to recharacterization under the abuse-of-law doctrine, ATAD CFC rules, and permanent establishment attribution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppressing corporate income tax returns, recording fictitious costs, or concealing taxable turnover from cloud payroll subscriptions; repeated non-filing after a formal notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full avoidance amount plus 0.20% monthly interest; penalty of 40% of additional tax after a formal demand (80% in cases of concealed activity); criminal fine of €15,000 or €30,000 and imprisonment of up to five years (CGI Article 1741).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The manager (gérant) and participants may be held jointly and severally liable; courts may lift the corporate veil, issue travel bans, freeze assets, and disqualify the director from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging disproportionate management fees, interest, or royalties to a French entity from a low-tax jurisdiction, or maintaining intercompany agreements without an arm's-length comparability analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment restating French taxable profits under Article 57 CGI; 0.20% monthly interest; additional 40% penalty for deliberate inaccuracies; failure to produce TP documentation triggers a penalty equal to 5% of the reassessed amount (minimum €10,000) under CGI Article 1735.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false transfer-pricing documents face personal liability for resulting tax liabilities and fines; severe cases may attract criminal sanctions for fiscal fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a SARL in France with no operational premises, no employees, and no actual decision-making, solely to obtain French PE status or treaty benefits, or to strip profits away from the French taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invocation of the fraudulent abuse-of-law procedure re-characterizes the arrangement and imposes an 80% penalty (or 40% if not fraudulent); the entity's registration may be cancelled and unpaid taxes become immediately due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers who set up or use a shell SARL may be declared jointly liable for understated corporate taxes; civil restitution petitions, asset attachments, and travel restrictions may be ordered; anti-money-laundering charges can also be brought.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register ultimate beneficial owners with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, or failing to perform anti-money-laundering checks on the payroll platform's payment rails (Direct Debit ACH / SWIFT Wire) despite the medium-risk enhanced category.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to €375,000 and imprisonment of five years for AML non-disclosure under the French Monetary and Financial Code; the RCS may order rectification and administrative injunctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners can be held personally liable for fines, compelled to surrender passports, and charged with money-laundering offenses if funds are laundered through programmed payroll payments; professional bans may be imposed.
